metadata.title: Upgraded ffish.js to 0.4.4 and added validate_fen()

issue_payload.body:
Hello @ianfab ,
I implemented an FEN validation method for **apiutil.h** as requested in #87.
+ FEN_VALIDATION validate_fen(const std::string& fen, const Variant* v)

The validation method returns either `FEN_OK` or one of **13** unique error codes.

```C++
enum FEN_VALIDATION : int {
  FEN_MISSING_SPACE_DELIM = -12,
  FEN_INVALID_NB_PARTS = -11,
  FEN_INVALID_CHAR = -10,
  FEN_FILE_SIZE_MISMATCH = -9,
  FEN_INVALID_NUMBER_OF_RANKS = -8,
  FEN_INVALID_POCKET_INFO = -7,
  FEN_INVALID_SIDE_TO_MOVE = -6,
  FEN_INVALID_CASTLING_INFO = -5,
  FEN_INVALID_EN_PASSANT_SQ = -4,
  FEN_INVALID_CHECK_COUNTER = -3,
  FEN_INVALID_HALF_MOVE_COUNTER = -2,
  FEN_INVALID_MOVE_COUTNER = -1,
  FEN_EMPTY = 0,
  FEN_OK = 1
};
```

Each starting fen is now validated in **test.js** including custom variants from **variants.ini**.
In the process of this, I found that `[]` was missing in the starting fen of _makrukhouse_, _xiangqihouse_, _janggihouse_ and _shogun_.
There is a test for each error code in **test.js**.

The following features were added to **ffish.js**:
+ **ffish.validate_fen(fen)** it validates a given chess fen and returns +1 if fen is valid. Otherwise an error code will be returned.
+ **ffish.validate_fen(fen, uciVariant)** it validates a given fen and returns +1 if fen is valid. Otherwise an error code will be returned.
+ **ffish.startingFen(uciVariant)** it returns the starting fen for the given uci-variant.
+ **board.pocket(turn)** it returns the pocket for the given player as a string with no delimeter. All pieces are returned in lower case.
+ uddated **ffish.js** and **ffish-es6** to **0.4.3**.

**Refactoring**
+ replaced logic of `bool first = true` by `save_pop_back(string& s)` to reduce code size.
+ replaced `s += " " + s2;` by `s += " "; s += s2;` to improve speed.

updated **README.md**
+ simplified memory specification
+ added `-std=c++17` to allow building with recent _NNUE_ code

@QueensGambit from one year experience on pychess site the most common cases of user defined invalid FENs are where rook or king positions contradict to castling rights or kings are touching or missing. See https://github.com/gbtami/pychess-variants/blob/master/client/chess.ts#L644
Can you add these additional checks to ffish.js please?

discussion_timeline.author: ianfab
discussion_timeline.body:
Thanks a lot! It will take me some time to think through all of the possible cases of FENs, so I will perhaps add CR comments step by step and not at once, so maybe you wait a bit with addressing them to save you time. A few initial remarks:
* Some of the startFENs were "intentionally" wrong, since I knew the parser supports those cases, but it makes sense to consolidate those now that we have a validation. The question is if the validator should only accept **the** correct FEN or also others that are accepted by the parser, but perhaps the former makes more sense in order to encourage sticking to standards while still being robust in cases where the validation is not used prior to inputting an FEN, e.g., for FEN differences between cutechess and XBoard, since XBoard e.g. skips en passant and castling fields for variants where they are not applicable. The latter example might also be relevant for checking the startFens, because I think I remember using XBoard style FENs sometimes.
* I could swear I added `-std=c++17` yesterday, but thanks for fixing that. I did not encounter any issues with ffish.js after the merge and seems you didn't either, so that is reaffirming that the NNUE code did not break anything.
* I will perhaps also add the FEN validation to pyffish and to the variant config validator after merging this, unless you want to add this yourself still in this PR.

discussion_timeline.author: QueensGambit
discussion_timeline.body:
> @QueensGambit from one year experience on pychess site the most common cases of user defined invalid FENs are where rook or king positions contradict to castling rights or kings are touching or missing. See https://github.com/gbtami/pychess-variants/blob/master/client/chess.ts#L644
> Can you add these additional checks to ffish.js please?

Regarding the additional checks.
There are a few variants where these checks need to be skipped:
* **giveaway_variant**, **antichess_variant**, **codrus_variant**: It is allowed to have multiple kings or no king.
* **clobber_variant**, **tictactoe_variant**, **connect4_variant**, **reversi_variant**: There is no king to begin with. Hence if there is no king in the starting fen, we can skip checking the number of kings.
* **atomic_variant**, **giveaway_variant**, **antichess_variant**, **codrus_variant**: It is allowed that kings touch.
* **chess960 (castling)**: Checking if the kings and rooks are still on starting squares is not possible because the starting fen is not directly available. However, you could check if the kings are between their rooks and on their starting rank.

The implementation of the **atomic_variant** is still missing (https://github.com/ianfab/Fairy-Stockfish/issues/81) but we need to keep this in mind for later.

discussion_timeline.author: ianfab
discussion_timeline.body:
In Fairy-SF it is impossible to have more than one (royal) king per side, the code does not support that scenario. Variants with non-royal kings use the commoner piece type, which is strictly separated in the code. So as long as validation code for the king is skipped if none is present (for the respective side), variants like giveaway do not affect such conditions, since the presence of a king is considered as optional in **all** variants, even chess or the like. Regarding the touching kings it is a bit more tricky, because one needs to consider that in Fairy-SF the `KING` piece type is just a placeholder for a royal piece type. The actual movement is determined by the `kingType`, which therefore needs to be considered when checking for "touching" (e.g., consider knightmate) kings.

Edit: Regarding atomic, you should not worry about that for now. It is more likely (if ever) to be implemented as an extinction variant with a non-royal king, since breaking the assumptions that an attack on the king is always a check would massively complicate maintenance, which I am mostly likely not going to do.

discussion_timeline.author: ianfab
discussion_timeline.body:
Apart from the comments I already wrote, it mostly looks good to me. Ensuring that an FEN is strictly valid is very challenging, so from my perspective it is fine to leave it at the checks you included so far, and then extend it later, therefore my comments mostly focus on avoiding false negatives. In order to have a good understanding of the limitations, I would however like to summarize what is not validated yet:
* Promoted pieces (i.e., does a `+...` piece really have a promoted form?)
* S-Chess gates
* Cambodian "gates"
* Consistency of castling rights and king/rook positions
* Legality of position (king of side to move in check, etc.)

discussion_timeline.body:
> [...] Ensuring that an FEN is strictly valid is very challenging, so from my perspective it is fine to leave it at the checks you included so far, and then extend it later, therefore my comments mostly focus on avoiding false negatives.

I concur. Aiming for low false negative rate is more important than reducing false positives here.
This method will most likely mainly be used for validating user inputs.
The variants also differ in popularity making some checks more important than others.
Some additional checks could be added later.

I'll revise the code based on your review.

discussion_timeline.author: QueensGambit
discussion_timeline.body:
I revised the code and added additional checks for _contradicting castling setups_, _touching kings_ and a check for _number of royal kings_ as requested by @gbtami .

The additional castling checks required a lot of more code. Therefore, I moved a lot of checks into separate functions to improve maintainability and readability.

All starting fens of all variants returned `FEN_OK`.
Despite, adding new test cases for possible failure cases, I ensured that all game positions of the example games returned `FEN_OK`.

discussion_timeline.author: ianfab
discussion_timeline.body: Thanks! To be honest I am not entirely happy about how some conditions are defined, because they seem to filter down the list of existing variants to the ones where it should apply rather than constructively defining the conditions from the bottom up based on the rules that are prerequisites. However, I can imagine that this perhaps is incredibly hard to do without having too much experience with the "rule space" of this engine (I should perhaps also improve documentation in that regard), and I do not want to unnecessarily hinder the merge of this feature, especially considering that it seems to work well for all existing variants. So if there are no objections I would then at a later point try to modify the conditions to a more bottom up approach, but merge this first version as is.

discussion_timeline.body:

discussion_timeline.author: yjf2002ghty
discussion_timeline.body: 1024 is just set for some enthusiasts who use a very high end CPU (e.g. Threadripper 7995WX) to go much deeper in solving one position. discussion_timeline.author: ianfab
discussion_timeline.body: Setting a very high max ply does have a downside in the fairly common case of a short forced mate. There the engine will quickly solve the position at low ply and then rush through all iterations until max ply without needing to do much more search. Since the new iterations do not really require new search (as TT has everything already), it won't consume that much CPU by the engine, but it will produce a lot more (fairly useless) output that needs to be communicated and parsed, which can e.g. put significant load on a GUI. Since this is the much more common scenario, in the rare case that someone is willing to put enourmous efforts into solving a long win, recompiling with a higher max ply shouldn't be a big deal.

discussion_timeline.author: yjf2002ghty

However on Python based GUIs like PyChess GUI and FairyFishGUI, the difference can be at most 3 seconds, probably due to the low performance issue of Python.
So it does compromise the experience of Python based GUIs , and limiting depth is necessary.

issue_payload.body:
Hello @ianfab ,

I created the initial version of **ffish.js** today, as discussed in https://github.com/ianfab/Fairy-Stockfish/issues/157.

The main functionality such as creating a new board from fen, loading a new fen, generating all legal moves (UCI or SAN) is covered. The syntax of **ffish.js** is similar to [python-chess](https://github.com/niklasf/python-chess).

Moreover, I moved some utility functions which are both used in **pyffish** and **ffish.js** to a new file called `apiutil.h`.

## Build instuctions

```bash
cd Fairy-Stockfish/src
```
```bash
emcc -O3 --bind ffishjs.cpp \
benchmark.cpp \
bitbase.cpp \
bitboard.cpp \
endgame.cpp \
evaluate.cpp \
material.cpp \
misc.cpp \
movegen.cpp \
movepick.cpp \
parser.cpp \
partner.cpp \
pawns.cpp \
piece.cpp \
position.cpp \
psqt.cpp \
search.cpp \
thread.cpp \
timeman.cpp \
tt.cpp \
uci.cpp \
syzygy/tbprobe.cpp \
ucioption.cpp \
variant.cpp \
xboard.cpp \
-o ../tests/js/ffish.js
```

## Exemplary usage in JavaScript

Load the API in JavaScript:

```javascript
const ffish = require('./ffish.js');
```

Create a new variant board from its default starting position:

```javascript
let board = new ffish.Board("chess");
```

Set a custom fen position:
```javascript
board.setFen("rnb1kbnr/ppp1pppp/8/3q4/8/8/PPPP1PPP/RNBQKBNR w KQkq - 0 3");
```

Initialize a board with a custom FEN:
```javascript
board = new ffish.Board("crazyhouse", "rnb1kb1r/ppp2ppp/4pn2/8/3P4/2N2Q2/PPP2PPP/R1B1KB1R/QPnp b KQkq - 0 6");
```

Pushing a new move to the board:
```javascript
board.push("g2g4");
```

Generate all legal moves in UCI and SAN notation:
```javascript
let legalMoves = board.legalMovesStr().split(" ");
let legalMovesSan = board.legalMovesSanStr().split(" ");

for (var i = 0; i < legalMovesSan.length; i++) {
    console.log(`${i}: ${legalMoves[i]}, ${legalMovesSan[i]}`);
}
```

## Performance

I conducted some initial performance test in comparision with [**chess.js**](https://github.com/jhlywa/chess.js) and [**crazyhouse.js**](https://github.com/jak3122/crazyhouse.js).

### Move generation of two example positions for 1k iterations
```javascript
Standard Chess
==================
Call to board.legalMoves() took 27.46  milliseconds.
Call to board.legalMovesStr()+legalMoves.split(" ") took 24.84  milliseconds.
board.legalMovesSanStr().split(" ").length: 29
Call to board.legalMovesSanStr()+legalMoves.split(" ") took 23.40  milliseconds.
chess.moves().length: 29
Call to chess.moves() took 880.41  milliseconds.
Crazyhouse
===========
board.legalMovesStr().split(" ").length: 97
Call to board.legalMoves() took 55.29  milliseconds.
crazyhouse.moves().length: 97
Call to crazyhouse.moves() took 10257.35  milliseconds.
```

**ffish.js** is **~35x** faster than **chess.js** and **~185x** faster than **crazyhouse.js** for SAN move generation.

You can find the code of the testing server here:
* https://github.com/QueensGambit/Fairy-Stockfish/tree/ffish_js/tests/js

Currently, there are two versions for generating the moves.

`board.legalMovesSan()` and `board.legalMovesSanStr()`. The former returns the moves as a vector of strings and the later as a concatenated string with whitespaces.
Surprisingly, the concatenated string plus a splitting operation is faster than the vector form as seen above.
If you agree, I suggest to remove the vector form then.

Another thing which I found odd, is that `board.legalMovesSanStr()` is slightly faster than generating the moves in UCI form by using `board.legalMovesStr()`.

## TODOs

There are still few important TODOs:
* Adding a `pushSan()` function which requires converting a SAN move to _Fairy-Stockfish's_ move representation
* Validating FEN strings
* Loading PGN files

I can imagine that a native _Stockfish_ or _Multi-Variant-Stockfish_ version **fish.js**/**mvfish.js** for standard chess is 15x/10x faster than **ffish.js**.

It might be interesting to run a performance comparision with the [lichess-Scala-API](https://github.com/ornicar/scalachess) then.
I saw that you also added a bughouse backend to _Fairy-Stockfish_. Lichess still doesn't support boughouse, so it could benefit from accessing your API via **ffish.js**.

discussion_timeline.author: ianfab
discussion_timeline.body:
Wow, that is awesome. The performance also sounds very promising, although I agree that most likely a pure fish.js version could perhaps be ~10x faster as also perft is ~10x faster, but considering the already quite good performance compared to other libraries it probably will not be the bottleneck anyway. Below I have some more feedback:

- The addition of the `ffishjs.cpp` breaks the existing appveyor builds
  - The MSVC build must exclude the new file, see https://github.com/ianfab/Fairy-Stockfish/blob/f712f6f2d455ebe570e406edc369d332d5d655ab/appveyor.yml#L35
  - The python extension also needs to exclude the new source file to work, see https://github.com/ianfab/Fairy-Stockfish/blob/f712f6f2d455ebe570e406edc369d332d5d655ab/setup.py#L27-L30
- For source files that are purely Fairy-Stockfish code and do not originate from official SF (as for apiutil.h) I usually use a different copyright header, see e.g., variant.h or the like.
- Including the building with emscripten and ideally also a few tests in the CI would be nice to avoid future regressions.
- SF source code usually uses the convention to have opening braces for if/for (not for functions, methods, or classes) on new lines, and to skip them if not required (for single statements).
- A simple stupid implementation of pushSan could be to just generate the list of legal SAN moves and compare the given string to them (same approach is used to parse coordinate notation, see https://github.com/ianfab/Fairy-Stockfish/blob/f712f6f2d455ebe570e406edc369d332d5d655ab/src/uci.cpp#L433-L435 This would of course neither be a very robust parsing (e.g., failing on optional disambiguation) nor the most performant, but might be sufficient for now.
- FEN validation is planned since it is also required for pyffish and the CECP protocol, see https://github.com/ianfab/Fairy-Stockfish/issues/87 (but I have not started on it yet).

The first point is the only one I see as a must to include in this PR, everything else can be optional and also be done at a later point.

- In the first if statement of the diff, `if (pos.side_to_move() == strongSide && (attacks_bb<KNIGHT>(NSq) & KSq))` is a bug. I think the intention is to see if the king is attacking the knight, so I fixed it to that.
- In some cases where the king is to move and it's on the edge (e.g., Kg1 and Ne2), the knight attacking the king actually does mean that the knight wins (but only if the king is not attacking any other squares the knight attacks). So I rewrote the code to handle all cases where the king and knight attack each other or share attacks.

Briefly tested with a few positions, but haven't done a fishtest (http://www.variantfishtest.org:6543/tests doesn't load for me).

discussion_timeline.author: ianfab
discussion_timeline.body:
I read this code again and as far as I can see it was fully intentional.

Scenario 1: If the knight attacks the king and the king is to move, the knight side always wins by premoving to the king square.
Scenario 2: If the king and knight attack a common square and the knight is to move, it can sacrifice itself on that square.

Scenario 2 seems to miss the scenario where the knight already attacks the king, apart from that it looks fine. And in case of mandatory captures pruning is generally skipped, so it is unlikely to be a problem.

Note that you can not use mate values in endgame evaluation, because it does not know about the current depth at which this position occurred (ss->ply).

Regarding fishtest, I put it down some time ago due to inactivity to save costs, and it likely won't come back.

Edit: One additional note. As the (somewhat brief) comment indicates, the general idea was to only catch the cases where the knight wins, because afterwards it assumes the king wins.

discussion_timeline.author: johndoknjas
discussion_timeline.body: @ianfab In scenario 1 though, we could have something like Ke4 and Nc5. Premoving Ne4 wouldn't work since the king can go to d3.

@ianfab I've applied your patch, thanks. There's also scenarios where a knight can beat a king anywhere on the edge. E.g., Ke1 and Nc2/Ng2, when it is the king to move. This also means any position with Ke1 and the knight a move away from c2/g2 will be a win for the knight, when it is its turn. I've added a new commit that tries to handle all cases where a knight can win (not sure how it'll behave in fishtest though).

For what I was talking about for the longer mate, this branch finds a mate in 8 by depth 18, and a mate in 7 by depth 21. For the master branch though, a mate in 7 is found by depth 15. After the newest 5afc03b commit though, mate in 7 is found at depth 17.

discussion_timeline.author: ianfab
discussion_timeline.body:
Thanks, right, I forgot about the other cases. However, there is a trade-off between complexity and accuracy, so I would like to stop before those non-trivial exceptions, as mentioned my own exclusion of corner kings already almost felt like overkill, although it at least codewise is simple. There is still search to handle the rest, it is sufficient to be a fairly decent heuristic. If we really want to make sure to avoid false win predictions, something simpler could be to just generalize the exception I made, like
```
-  if (!(KSq & (SQ_A1 | SQ_A8 | SQ_H1 | SQ_H8)))
+  if (!(KSq & (FileABB | FileHBB | Rank1BB | Rank8BB)))
```
I think there isn't any case with a king not on the edge that doesn't win (apart from the conditions captured before already), so that would keep it conservative and still fairly simple.


As a side note, I think we are using different testing conditions (I use `./stockfish bench antichess 16 1 25 test.epd` with the FEN `n7/8/8/8/8/8/8/7K w - - 0 1` in the test.epd), as for me the latest version finds mate later than the commit before. I don't know of any other variant than kono yet that is using blockers of flag squares, so it is difficult for me to foresee how to best generalize this to make it reusable, since there are multiple ways how to interpret kono as a special case of a more general concept. Open questions e.g. are:
* What should be counted as a blocker? Any occupancy (including own pieces and walls), only opponent pieces, or only specific opponent pieces?
* Since in kono the flag piece count equals the number of flag squares, how should this be treated in the general case? Are we counting blockers always, or only after falling below the required count of free squares (equivalent to what you have now)? Like `flag piece count >= max(required count - blockers, 1)` vs `flag piece count >= max(min(required count, flag square count - blockers), 1)`.

A small note with regards to performance. Since popcount can potentially be slow depending on hardware, it is best to avoid when not needed. E.g., `popcount(b) >= 1` is equivalent to just `b` in a boolean context, and `popcount(b) == 0` is the same as `!b`.

discussion_timeline.author: RainRat
discussion_timeline.body:
I looked over the Zillions library (breakthrough/race types in specific) and did not find another where blocked piece=win. Usually the rules obligate a move or adjudicate it a different way. If one really wanted to deep dive, they could look into some of the other games that obligate a move and come up with some different generalizations for that.

So, currently, the criteria is if at least one flag piece is in the flag zone and none of the squares were *empty*.
-If you had a game with flag pieces and non-flag pieces, AND you got one flag piece in the zone AND you filled the rest with your non-flag pieces, then this option would adjudicate as a win. This is admittedly not ideal.
-Wall squares are not empty squares, so they would be considered blocking.
 
I can possibly look at more games to find more ways to generalize, but with just one example, It's hard to generalize.

[breakthrough survey.txt](https://github.com/fairy-stockfish/Fairy-Stockfish/files/11256333/breakthrough.survey.txt)

Thanks a lot for the research and updates. Functionality-wise it looks good to me, but I have some concerns regarding the implementation of the game end conditions. In general it is good practice keep things separate and explicit, so what you wrote makes sense. However, Fairy-Stockfish is very feature heavy and subject to further extension, so I try to reduce the complexity in terms of number of code paths as much as possible, even if that makes the individual code paths maybe a bit harder to read, as it can otherwise quickly get out of hand with many rule configuration options when you try to allow arbitrary combination of rules. This is quite specific to this project and maybe also debatable, but so far this works best for me in this project to keep it maintainable.

Therefore I would like to rather implement the conditions in a similar (though not necessarily identical) way as my formulas/pseudo-code above. However, I appreciate your efforts and don't like to ask you now to rewrite your functional code. So depending on what you prefer you could either try to update it yourself according to what I am describing if you are interested, or I would also be fine to merge it as is, and then would do the refactoring myself at a later point.

One convenient feature would be to allow a missing 50-move rule and full move counter.
In that case, we assume a 50-move rule counter of 0 and a full move counter as 1.
This is also possible on lichess.org.

e.g. `4b1k1/1p3p2/4pPp1/p2pP1P1/P2P4/1P1B4/8/2K5 w - -`
and `4b1k1/1p3p2/4pPp1/p2pP1P1/P2P4/1P1B4/8/2K5 w - - 0`
will be interpreted as a valid FEN and result in 
`4b1k1/1p3p2/4pPp1/p2pP1P1/P2P4/1P1B4/8/2K5 w - - 0 1`.

This behavior would also require some changes to the `FEN_INVALID_NB_PARTS` check.

Additionally, if the side to move information is missing as well, we could assume that it is White's turn to move, again same as on lichess.org.

e.g. `4b1k1/1p3p2/4pPp1/p2pP1P1/P2P4/1P1B4/8/2K5`
will be interpreted as a valid FEN and result in 
`4b1k1/1p3p2/4pPp1/p2pP1P1/P2P4/1P1B4/8/2K5 w - - 0 1`.

**Edit:** I just noticed, that Stockfish assumes Black's turn to move, if the move counter is missing.
https://github.com/ianfab/Fairy-Stockfish/blob/master/src/position.cpp#L310
I think this is fine as well.

Do you by chance know whether there is any (well-known) GUI that does not send the time/otim commands to sync the clocks? I am asking because SF does not keep track of the time at all, it just relies on that the GUI always sends the time command.

discussion_timeline.author: alwey
discussion_timeline.body:
AFAIK fairly recent UIs that support Xboard protocol V2 will send `time` / `otim` if `feature time=1`, which is the default.  Perhaps it would be good to issue `feature .... time=1` explicitely.

The initial mechanism for time control is based on the `level` command and Xboard-engines were expected to have their own time measurement, especially protocol V1 engines. So this is an example of the fact that UCI engines are simpler and Xboard engines are more complex.
